Re: Protest of Proposed 765 kV Transmission Line Project
Applicant: Oncor Electric Delivery Company / Lower Colorado River Authority
Docket No.: 59475
To the Public Utility Commission of Texas:
I submit this formal protest regarding the proposed 765 kV transmission line project that would impact Concho and McCulloch Counties, Texas.
As a person that frequents this area for agritourism purposes, I am directly affected by the proposed routing of this project. The intrusion of this transmission line would limit my ability to pursue activities on the affected properties.  This will also have a negative economic impact on surrounding towns and businesses as I would have to take my business elsewhere.
LEGAL BASIS FOR PROTEST
1. Failure to Satisfy Certificate of Convenience and Necessity (CCN) Requirements
Under Texas Utilities Code §37.051–§37.056, a utility must obtain or amend a Certificate of Convenience and Necessity (CCN) prior to constructing a transmission line. 
The Commission is required to evaluate:
Need for service
Adequacy of existing infrastructure
Community values and environmental integrity
Use of existing rights-of-way
Alignment with property boundaries and land use
There is insufficient evidence that this project meets these statutory criteria, particularly with respect to:
Use of existing corridors
Minimization of impacts to rural landowners
Demonstrated necessity versus alternatives
2. Violation of PUC Routing Criteria (Substantive Rule §25.101)
The Commission must evaluate routing based on:
Prudent avoidance of EMF exposure
Community, aesthetic, and environmental impacts
Use of compatible rights-of-way 
The proposed route through Concho and McCulloch Counties appears inconsistent with these requirements by:
Introducing new corridors rather than co-locating infrastructure
Creating disproportionate burdens on rural landowners
Failing to adequately mitigate visual and environmental harm
3. Property Rights and Eminent Domain Concerns
Texas law grants utilities eminent domain authority to acquire easements if negotiations fail.
However, this authority is contingent upon lawful CCN approval and proper route selection. The proposed routing:
Imposes long-term restrictions on agricultural land use
Reduces property values
Creates permanent encumbrances on private land
4. Failure to Adequately Consider Environmental and Agricultural Impacts
PUC rules require consideration of environmental integrity and land use impacts. 
In Concho and McCulloch Counties, this includes:
Disruption to ranching, farming, and agritourism operations
Soil erosion risks in fragile rangeland
Wildlife habitat fragmentation
5. Inadequate Public Participation and Rural Impact Equity
The routing process must incorporate meaningful landowner input and equitable burden distribution.
Concho and McCulloch County landowners appear to bear disproportionate impacts relative to urban beneficiaries.
REQUEST FOR RELIEF
I respectfully request that the Commission:
Deny the proposed routing through Concho and McCulloch Counties.
Require full evaluation of co-location alternatives along existing corridors.
Mandate a comprehensive Environmental Impact Assessment.
Require demonstration of necessity under §37.056.
Ensure compliance with prudent avoidance standards.
Respectfully submitted,
[Your Signature]
